Scope of this page



What: 2025 line-point resurvey of 1991 EIR / 1999 Revegetation Plan mitigation parcels—cover and composition against Table 2 goals (Los Angeles Department of Water and Power 1999).
Why: Separate from Laws Type E (2003). Partners need a transparent path from segment hits → site goals. Pages marked (draft) elsewhere are prototypes; this report is the working 1999-plan monitoring product.

title: 1999 Plan Revegetation Monitoring (2025)
text:
This report covers 1991 EIR / 1999 Revegetation Plan mitigation parcels re-surveyed in August 2025: IND105, IND123, IND131N/S, BLK16E, TIN054, BGP160E/W, BIS097, and LAW118. It is separate from the Type E transfer (2003) sites and their reference sites.
Raw data come from Re_Veg Parcels 2025 IND_BLK_TIN_BGP_BIS_LAW.xlsx. We parse species hit counts only — staff %COV, %COMP, accuracy, and other calculated columns in that workbook are not used.
Percent cover is computed as hits / n_possible_hits × 100, where n_possible_hits = segment length (m) / 0.5 m intercept spacing. Segment lengths come from GIS distance between post endpoints (data/transect_segment_denominators.csv). That GIS denominator is the best available when field sheets did not record total possible points. Field practice for 2025 is still being confirmed with staff: protocol implies a first-hit every 0.5 m, but some years (including 2017/2025 for some parcels) may have been tallied per segment without point locations. Segments are typically defined by walking between GPS’d posts; t-posts should be present but were not always found. Goal outcomes are summarized in Table 1; spatial context is in Fig. 6.

title: 1999 Plan Revegetation Monitoring (2025)
text:
1999 Revegetation Plan goals
What the Plan requires (Los Angeles Department of Water and Power 1999): site-specific live native perennial cover, composition (species contributing to cover), and recruitment / sustainability (≥25% of vegetation cover as natural recruits ≥3 years old).
What this report scores: cover and composition from 2025 LPI (with the master-workbook CI rules below). Sustainability is not scored from LPI alone here; the LADWP aerial pilot is summarized next as context for that third criterion.
Goals below follow Table 2 (2021–22 Mitigation Projects and Status).

LADWP proposal — aerial recruitment / sustainability (2026)
What: A remote-sensing workflow (high-res imagery + LiDAR → live/dead/bare → interannual overlap) to estimate recruit share of live cover on IND105.
Why summarize it here: The Plan’s 25% recruit rule needs an operational definition; this pilot is the current LA proposal. Full deck remains local (reveg1999plan-docs/); County dual-track notes in docs/1999plan_sustainability_monitoring_proposal.md.
Why IND105: cover and composition already met—useful for testing sustainability; IND123 is also of interest for full completion.

Workflow (slides 7–8)

Establish “current” vegetation from 0.05 m imagery + LiDAR (August 2022).

Georeference (spline).

Object recognition (eCognition).

Random Forest → Bare Ground / Live Vegetation / Dead Vegetation.

Merge and explode live polygons.

Superimpose year-of-interest live polygons on a prior year.

New recruits = no overlap with prior live cover, or overlapping area < 10% of the polygon (also: previously undetectable, < 0.3 m).

Annual issue (slide 13): 2017 RS cannot separate annuals; IND106 T10/T12 (within IND105) had 25.7% annual hits → scale cover × 0.743; keep non-intersecting polygons that overlap 2022 live or dead.
Caveats from LA watershed resources staff: Annuals inflate recruitment area. If credited as recruitment in 2017 but empty in 2022, drop from the 25% share (annual signal; perennial mortality is an alternate assumption). Lateral growth ≠ recruitment on LPI alone; sample ≠ whole site without a sampling frame.


Recommendations (slide 17)

Acquire high-resolution remote sensing (~0.05 m / 5 cm) with LiDAR every three to five years. (Deck text says “< 0.05 cm” — treat as typo for 0.05 m, matching the 2022 acquisition.)

Conduct ground monitoring concurrently with RS acquisition.

Going forward (ICWD): treat 2022 as baseline; compare expected 2024 3DEP LiDAR to 2022 and to 2025 transects; refine baseline before the next high-res flight.
Compliance method (from LADWP 1991 EIR REVEGETATION DATA-MASTER.xlsm): cover is met when the upper 80% confidence interval of mean transect cover reaches 90% of the Table 2 cover goal (upper CI80 ≥ 0.9 × goal). Species composition is met when observed richness reaches 75% of the Table 2 species goal. The 80% CI uses mean + t₀.₉,ₙ₋₁ × SD / √n across transects (or segments, for 2025).
This report compares 2025 live native perennial cover, upper 80% CI, and native perennial species with ≥3 hits to those targets. Cover and species metrics use the same perennial filter as the LADWP master workbook (Lifecycle contains “Perennial”). Parcels with missing segment lengths (denominators) are marked incomplete.
Parcel boundaries: AGOL polygons only — no transect buffering. Most parcels use mitigation_sites.shp; LAW118 uses mitigation_view_polygons.geojson; TIN054 uses the experimental plot in data/gis/TIN054.json. TIN054 transect geometry is TBD (current post pairing draws incorrectly; map left blank until remapped).

title: Laws Type E Transfer Revegetation
text:
Scope of this page



What: Working compliance report for Laws Type E transfer parcels under the 2003 revegetation plan (Los Angeles Department of Water and Power 2003a, 2003b).
Why: Annual cover and composition scores are the decision artifacts partners need; publishing them with methods makes the path from hits → goals auditable. Pages marked (draft) elsewhere are prototypes—see goals & caps summary for shared direction vs the open ATTO/ERNA cap question.

title: Laws Type E Transfer Revegetation
text:
These parcels are Type E transfers: land taken out of Type E irrigated agriculture and managed toward a precipitation-dependent natural community, not remaining in agricultural use. Under the 2003 Laws Revegetation Plan this report tracks LAW090, LAW094, LAW095, and LAW118/LAW129. Companion reference parcel analyses support ATTO/ERNA capping. Other 1991 EIR / 1999 Plan sites are reported separately (1999 Plan monitoring).
Dryland revegetation toward a climax (or stable late-successional) state can take decades. Cover and composition goals are milestones along that path; succession thinking and longer-term forecasting matter alongside annual compliance snapshots. See STM (gravelly loam + abandoned-ag state) and NMDS (reference vs reveg composition). A LADWP draft amendment (July 2026) is under County review. Default tables use working caps; Cap scenarios compares LADWP draft and lower/higher cut points without replacing the primary analysis.
Revegetation Targets:

Perennial Cover ≥ 10%: Parcel-average native perennial cover from list of allowed species, with specific capping implemented for ATTO, ERNA10 and ATPO.
Species with ≥3 Hits ≥ 6: At least six perennial species with 3+ hits - from list of allowed species plus ATTO, ERNA10 and ATPO.
Species Richness ≥ 10: At least 10 distinct perennial species from list of allowed species plus ATTO, ERNA10 and ATPO
Transect Cover ≥ 2%: Each transect must have ≥2% perennial cover from list of allowed species plus ATTO, ERNA10 and ATPO
Grass Species Present: At least one grass species per parcel from list of allowed species

Capping Rules (working default): LAW090/094/095 — ATTO and ERNA10 at 0.3% each (ATPO uncapped on LAW090). LAW118/129 — ATTO/ERNA10 at 2% each, ATPO at 3%. Other cut points (LADWP draft, lower/higher) are parameterized in data/cap_scenarios.csv — see Cap scenarios.
Overall Target Achievement: Requires ALL targets to be met (cover AND richness AND transect coverage AND grass presence)
Legend: ✓ = Target attained | ✗ = Target not attained


Target 1: Perennial Cover ≥ 10% - Calculation: Sum hits for all allowable species per transect, convert to percentage cover - Formula: (hits / 200) × 100 per transect, then average across parcel - Capping: Apply species-specific limits before final calculation - Threshold: Final cover must be ≥ 10%
Target 2: Species with ≥3 Hits ≥ 6 - Method: Count species with 3+ hits from allowed species list - Process: Identify species meeting threshold, count total - Threshold: Must have at least 6 species with 3+ hits
Target 3: Species Richness ≥ 10 - Method: Count distinct perennial species from allowed species list - Process: Count unique species present in parcel - Threshold: Must have at least 10 distinct species
Target 4: Transect Cover ≥ 2% - Method: Calculate cover for each individual transect - Process: Ensure each transect meets 2% threshold - Assessment: Calculate compliance rate as percentage of transects meeting threshold
Target 5: Grass Species Present - Method: Verify at least one grass species per parcel - Process: Check for grass species from allowed species list - Assessment: Mark as compliant if any grass species found

Step 1: Load and Combine Data Sources
LAW090/094/095 Parcels (2022-2025) - Load from LADWP Excel file covering 2022-2025 - Species hits zeroed if not on allowed species list - Cover conversion: cover = hits × (1/200) × 100 - Raw hits converted to percentage cover for analysis

Data Integration - Apply uniform naming conventions and cover calculations - Ensure consistent data structure across all parcel-year combinations - Validate data completeness and quality

# Load ALL data from LawsRevegetationData Excel file (Species List Data sheet)
# This file contains LAW090, LAW094, LAW095 for all years (2022-2025)
data_law909495 <- read_excel("data/LawsRevegetationData_SummaryTable_2025_ForICWD092525.xlsx", 
                             sheet = "Species List Data") %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  select(parcel, year, transect, species, cover) %>%
  rename(hits = cover) %>%  # Rename cover to hits for consistency
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    transect = as.character(transect),  # Ensure transect is character
    species = str_trim(species)  # Remove leading/trailing spaces from species names
  ) %>%
  filter(year >= 2022 & year <= 2025) 
# %>%

# Load LAW118/129 2025 data from CSV (different format)
# This file has a special format with metadata in first 3 rows
# Read without headers to preserve the raw structure

                          col_names = FALSE,
                          show_col_types = FALSE)

# Extract metadata from first 3 rows

# Row 2: Transect numbers  
# Row 3: Bearing numbers

# Process species data (rows 4+)
species_data <- law118_129_raw[4:nrow(law118_129_raw), ]

# Create the long format data for LAW118/129 manually
law118_129_processed <- data.frame()

# Loop through each species (rows 4+)
for (i in 1:nrow(species_data)) {
  species_name <- as.character(species_data[i, 1])
  
  # Loop through each transect (columns 2+)
  for (j in 2:ncol(species_data)) {
    hits_value <- as.numeric(species_data[i, j])
    
    if (!is.na(hits_value) && hits_value > 0) {
      # Create a row for this species-transect combination
      # Combine LAW118 and LAW129 into single "LAW118/129" parcel
      parcel_name <- ifelse(parcel_names[j-1] %in% c("LAW118", "LAW129"), "LAW118/129", parcel_names[j-1])
      
      # Create unique transect identifier by combining parcel and transect number
      unique_transect <- paste0(parcel_names[j-1], "_", transect_numbers[j-1])
      
      new_row <- data.frame(
        parcel = parcel_name,
        year = 2025,
        transect = unique_transect,
        species = str_trim(species_name),
        hits = hits_value
      )
      
      law118_129_processed <- bind_rows(law118_129_processed, new_row)
    }
  }
}

# Combine all data
data_combined <- bind_rows(data_law909495, law118_129_processed)

# Fix parcel naming for consistency - combine LAW118 and LAW129 into "LAW118/129"
data_combined <- data_combined %>%
  mutate(
    parcel = case_when(
      parcel == "LAW129" & year == 2022 ~ "LAW118/129",
      parcel == "LAW118" & year == 2023 ~ "LAW118/129",  # Add LAW118 2023 to LAW118/129
      TRUE ~ parcel
    )
  )

# Cap scenarios (working default + LADWP draft + lower/higher sensitivity)
cap_scenarios <- read_csv("data/cap_scenarios.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
DEFAULT_CAP_SCENARIO <- "working"

parcel_group_for <- function(parcel) {
  if (parcel %in% c("LAW090", "LAW094", "LAW095")) {
    "LAW90_94_95"
  } else if (parcel %in% c("LAW118/129", "LAW118", "LAW129")) {
    "LAW118_129"
  } else {
    NA_character_
  }
}

lookup_cap <- function(scenario, parcel, species) {
  grp <- parcel_group_for(parcel)
  hit <- cap_scenarios %>%
    filter(
      .data$scenario == !!scenario,
      .data$parcel_group == !!grp,
      .data$species == !!species
    )
  if (nrow(hit) == 0) {
    return(NA_real_) # no row → uncapped
  }
  as.numeric(hit$cap_pct[[1]])
}

# Function to calculate cover and capping for a parcel/year
calculate_parcel_cover <- function(parcel, year, scenario = DEFAULT_CAP_SCENARIO) {
  # Handle LAW118/129 as combined parcel
  if (parcel == "LAW118/129") {
    # Get data for LAW118/129 (already combined in data processing)
    parcel_data <- data_filtered %>%
      filter(parcel == "LAW118/129", year == !!year)
    # Get original data for transect counting
    original_parcel_data <- data_combined %>%
      filter(parcel == "LAW118/129", year == !!year)
  } else {
    # Get data for this specific parcel/year
    parcel_data <- data_filtered %>%
      filter(parcel == !!parcel, year == !!year)
    # Get original data for transect counting
    original_parcel_data <- data_combined %>%
      filter(parcel == !!parcel, year == !!year)
  }
  
  if (nrow(parcel_data) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Determine which species list to use
  allowable_species_codes <- if (parcel %in% c("LAW090", "LAW094", "LAW095")) {
    allowable_species_combined %>% 
      filter(parcel_group == "LAW90_94_95") %>% 
      pull(species)
  } else if (parcel == "LAW118/129") {
    allowable_species_combined %>% 
      filter(parcel_group == "LAW118_129") %>% 
      pull(species)
  } else {
    character(0)
  }
  
  # Filter to only allowable species
  parcel_allowable <- parcel_data %>%
    filter(species %in% allowable_species_codes)
  
  # Debug: Show species filtering for LAW118/129 2025
  if (parcel == "LAW118/129" && year == 2025 && scenario == DEFAULT_CAP_SCENARIO) {
    cat("\n=== Species Filtering for", parcel, year, "===\n")
    cat("Allowable species codes:", paste(allowable_species_codes, collapse = ", "), "\n")
    cat("Species in data before filtering:", paste(unique(parcel_data$species), collapse = ", "), "\n")
    cat("Species after filtering:", paste(unique(parcel_allowable$species), collapse = ", "), "\n")
    excluded_species <- setdiff(unique(parcel_data$species), unique(parcel_allowable$species))
    if (length(excluded_species) > 0) {
      cat("EXCLUDED species (not allowable):", paste(excluded_species, collapse = ", "), "\n")
    }
  }
  
  # Calculate original cover (sum of all species cover)
  n_transects <- n_distinct(original_parcel_data$transect)
  original_cover <- if(nrow(parcel_allowable) > 0) {
    # Convert hits to cover: hits / 200 * 100
    total_cover_percent <- sum(parcel_allowable$hits / 200 * 100)
    parcel_average_cover <- total_cover_percent / n_transects
    
    # Debug: Show calculation for LAW118/129 2025
    if (parcel == "LAW118/129" && year == 2025 && scenario == DEFAULT_CAP_SCENARIO) {
      cat("\n=== Cover Calculation Debug for", parcel, year, "===\n")
      cat("Number of transects:", n_transects, "\n")
      cat("Parcel average cover:", round(parcel_average_cover, 2), "%\n")
      cat("Species breakdown (before capping):\n")
      species_breakdown <- parcel_allowable %>% 
        group_by(species) %>% 
        summarise(total_hits = sum(hits), .groups = 'drop') %>%
        mutate(
          total_cover_percent = round(total_hits / 200 * 100, 2),
          species_avg_cover = round(total_cover_percent / n_transects, 2)
        ) %>%
        arrange(desc(species_avg_cover))
      print(species_breakdown)
    }
    
    parcel_average_cover
  } else {
    0
  }
  
  # Apply capping rules from cap_scenarios for this scenario
  if(nrow(parcel_allowable) > 0) {
    parcel_species_cover <- parcel_allowable %>%
      group_by(species) %>%
      summarise(
        total_hits = sum(hits),
        .groups = 'drop'
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        species_cover = (total_hits / 200 * 100) / n_transects,
        cap_pct = vapply(species, function(sp) lookup_cap(scenario, parcel, sp), numeric(1)),
        capped_cover = ifelse(is.na(cap_pct), species_cover, pmin(species_cover, cap_pct))
      )
    
    
    # Calculate final cover after capping
    final_cover <- sum(parcel_species_cover$capped_cover)
    
    # Debug: Show capping results for LAW118/129 2025
    if (parcel == "LAW118/129" && year == 2025 && scenario == DEFAULT_CAP_SCENARIO) {
      cat("\n=== Species Capping Results for", parcel, year, "===\n")
      capping_results <- parcel_species_cover %>%
        mutate(
          capping_applied = ifelse(species_cover != capped_cover, "YES", "NO"),
          reduction = round(species_cover - capped_cover, 2)
        ) %>%
        arrange(desc(capped_cover))
      print(capping_results)
      cat("Final cover after capping:", round(final_cover, 2), "%\n")
    }
  } else {
    final_cover <- 0
  }
  
  result <- data.frame(
    Parcel = parcel,
    Year = year,
    Scenario = scenario,
    `Cover %` = round(original_cover, 2),
    `Transects` = n_transects,
    `Cover After Species Caps` = round(final_cover, 2),
    `Allowed Sp Count` = n_distinct(parcel_allowable$species),
    `Cover Status` = ifelse(final_cover >= 10, "✅ Compliant", "❌ Non-compliant"),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  
  return(result)
}

# Function to calculate transect-level cover
calculate_transect_cover <- function(parcel_name, year_value, allowable_species_codes) {
  # Filter data for specific parcel and year
  parcel_data <- data_combined %>%
    filter(parcel == parcel_name, year == year_value)
  
  if (nrow(parcel_data) == 0) {
    return(data.frame(
      parcel = character(0),
      year = integer(0),
      transect = character(0),
      total_hits = numeric(0),
      cover_percentage = numeric(0),
      meets_2_percent = logical(0)
    ))
  }
  
  # Calculate cover for each transect
  transect_cover <- parcel_data %>%
    # Filter to only allowable species
    filter(species %in% allowable_species_codes) %>%
    group_by(transect) %>%
    summarise(
      total_hits = sum(hits, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = 'drop'
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      # Convert hits to cover percentage (hits/200 * 100)
      cover_percentage = (total_hits / 200) * 100,
      meets_2_percent = cover_percentage >= 2.0,
      parcel = parcel_name,
      year = year_value
    ) %>%
    select(parcel, year, transect, total_hits, cover_percentage, meets_2_percent)
  
  return(transect_cover)
}

# Function to calculate species with 3+ hits for each parcel and year
calculate_species_3plus_hits <- function(parcel_name, year_value, allowable_species_codes) {
  # Filter data for specific parcel and year
  parcel_data <- data_combined %>%
    filter(parcel == parcel_name, year == year_value)
  
  if (nrow(parcel_data) == 0) {
    return(data.frame(
      parcel = parcel_name,
      year = year_value,
      species_3plus_count = 0,
      meets_6_species = FALSE,
      species_3plus_list = "None"
    ))
  }
  
  # Calculate species with 3+ hits (allowable species only)
  species_3plus <- parcel_data %>%
    # Filter to only allowable species
    filter(species %in% allowable_species_codes) %>%
    group_by(species) %>%
    summarise(
      total_hits = sum(hits, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = 'drop'
    ) %>%
    filter(total_hits >= 3) %>%
    arrange(desc(total_hits))
  
  # Create summary
  species_3plus_count <- nrow(species_3plus)
  meets_6_species <- species_3plus_count >= 6
  species_3plus_list <- if(species_3plus_count > 0) {
    paste(species_3plus$species, collapse = ", ")
  } else {
    "None"
  }
  
  return(data.frame(
    parcel = parcel_name,
    year = year_value,
    species_3plus_count = species_3plus_count,
    meets_6_species = meets_6_species,
    species_3plus_list = species_3plus_list
  ))
}

title: Laws 2003 Plan Amendment (draft)
text:
Introduction
This amendment addresses deviations from the original 2003 Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) Revegetation Plan (the Plan) for the “Irrigation Project in the Laws Area” that occurred during implementation of the revegetation project. The amendment does not alter the fundamental purpose of the project, reduce mitigation obligations, or relax success criteria. Rather, it clarifies monitoring, species composition, and decision pathways based on implementation experience to ensure that mitigation remains enforceable and effective under California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).
Three main deviations are addressed as summarized in the table below:







Language in MND Revegetation Plan
Deviation




1. “Absent Technical Group approval, these species are the only ones to be planted on these three [or this] parcel[s]”
Species planted in the parcels that were not on approved species lists (see MND Table 1 and Table 2)


2. “Vegetation cover and composition consistent with the revegetation goal for each parcel is to be obtained by 2013”
Timeline exceeded as LADWP, working in good faith with Inyo County Water Department (ICWD), continued revegetation efforts


3. “Staff from LADWP and from the ICWD will jointly site the permanent transects, will jointly conduct monitoring using the transects, and will jointly analyze data …”
Initial siting and monitoring of the permanent transects was conducted by LADWP prior to joint ICWD involvement



[Pilot reference parcel monitoring was designed and implemented by LADWP prior to joint involvement in 2025 between LADWP and ICWD, though this monitoring was not directed in the MND explicitly.]
The 2003 MND provides guidance for project revegetation in the Plan, including two tables that recommend species for specific parcels. Table 1 lists species for parcels LAW090, 094, and 095, while Table 2 covers parcels LAW118/129. The Plan states that only these species can be planted unless approved by the Technical Group. However, some unlisted species have been planted or naturally recruited, especially in areas with drip irrigation, which encourages growth in wetter soils. This unintended recruitment is likely inevitable.
Due to the highly degraded state of the Laws parcels (MWH, 2004 & 2006), Torrey’s saltbush (Atriplex torreyi) and rubber rabbitbrush (Ericameria nauseosa) were planted in LAW090, 094, 095, and rubber rabbitbrush was planted at LAW118/129 as means to stabilize the site and jumpstart recovery (see Appendix F).
The MND outlined species to be planted within the parcels in its Revegetation Plan, in Tables 1 and 2. During implementation, additional species were planted without formal Technical Group approval (see Appendix F). On average, about 20% of plantings in Laws 90, 94, 95 and about 15% in Laws 118/129 included species not listed on the appropriate species planting list. Revegetation efforts extended beyond the original 2013 target, and initial monitoring protocols were implemented prior to joint review. Finally, revegetation parcel monitoring occurred without input from the County which resulted in the parcels being deemed “complete” without Technical Group approval.
The 2003 MND identified species for the revegetation parcels based on available data and ecological understanding at that time. Subsequent field observations and scientific literature demonstrate that Torrey’s saltbush and rubber rabbitbrush are naturally occurring components of comparable, undisturbed desert plant communities in the Laws area. Based on reference parcel observations and available literature, this amendment evaluates whether accounting of these species toward revegetation success is appropriate within defined limits.
This amendment is limited in scope and addresses only the potential inclusion of Torrey’s saltbush and rubber rabbitbrush. Other species not listed in the 2003 planting tables are not approved or authorized by this amendment to count toward revegetation success unless expressly approved through the Technical Group process. The amendment does not constitute a blanket approval of all species that may have been planted within the parcels.
This amendment includes: 1) defining the monitoring methodologies for both the revegetation parcels and the Plan’s reference parcels, 2) support for the addition of Torrey’s saltbush (ATTO) and rubber rabbitbrush (ERNA10) to the species lists, 3) modifying the revegetation goals with the inclusion of these species, 4) LADWP’s responsibilities if goals are not met, 5) defining LADWP’s obligations to the Plan in the event of a natural disturbance (such as wildfire or debris flow), and 6) a cleanup and reporting plan.

title: Laws 2003 Plan Amendment (draft)
text:
Background
The 2003 MND for the Irrigation Project in the Laws Area, adopted pursuant to CEQA, included a Revegetation Plan establishing vegetation cover and composition goals for lands removed from irrigation. The Plan applied to Laws Parcels LAW090, 094, 095, and 129, and a portion of LAW118.
Vegetation cover and species composition goals were developed using Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) Ecological Site Descriptions and vegetation inventory data collected by LADWP between 1984 and 1987 on City lands in the Owens Valley. The Plan established a minimum total native perennial cover of 10% and required species composition thresholds as follows:

LAW090, 094, and 095: at least 10 native perennial species, including one native grass.
LAW129 and the relevant portion of LAW118: at least eight native perennial species, including one native grass. As of the writing of this amendment, monitoring has occurred as follows: LAW090, 094, and 095 were monitored in 2022, 2024, 2025 and 2026; LAW129 was sampled in 2022; the portion of LAW118 surrounding LAW129 was sampled in 2023; and the combined parcel was sampled in 2025 and 2026.

This amendment will undergo CEQA review consistent with applicable guidelines.

title: Laws 2003 Plan Amendment (draft)
text:
Monitoring Methods

Revegetation parcel transect placement
LADWP established permanent transects to provide representative parcel-scale estimates while minimizing alignment bias with planted rows. Detailed transect siting, orientation, and field protocols are provided in Appendix B.


Reference parcel monitoring
Reference parcel monitoring was conducted to characterize vegetation composition and cover in parcels identified in the 2003 Plan as ecological benchmarks. Detailed reference parcel monitoring methods, including transect design, Landsat alignment, sampling intensity, and data handling procedures, are provided in Appendix C. Reference parcel maps and data tables are provided in Appendices D and E, respectively.


Monitoring LAW090
The Plan specified 30 equal-sized monitoring sections for LAW090. During implementation, LADWP segmented the parcel into 20 sections to accommodate parcel geometry and planted-row patterns. Because this differed from the original specification, an evaluation was conducted to determine whether use of 20 versus 30 transects materially affected parcel-level conclusions.
Results from field observations and supporting analyses indicated that estimates derived from 20 and 30 transects were comparable and did not materially alter determinations regarding revegetation performance. Accordingly, the difference between 20 and 30 transects is considered not material to management outcomes, and future monitoring may proceed using either sample size as jointly agreed through the Technical Group process. Detailed statistical evaluation of sampling configuration and analysis supporting the 2022 determination are provided in Appendix A.


Monitoring LAW118/129
In 2022, LADWP established 20 monitoring transects within LAW118/129 and in 2023, 15 additional transects were added to LAW118, increasing the total to 35. In 2025, LADWP and ICWD agreed to merge LAW118 and LAW129 into a single monitoring parcel and selected 20 transects from the existing network to align with the monitoring framework described in the plan. The selected transects will be used for future monitoring. Detailed transect selection and spatial distribution procedures are provided in Appendix B.


Reference Parcel Monitoring
To determine whether to include species not originally listed in the MND in the assessment of mitigation success, species presence and cover across other Type A (i.e. with evapotranspiration requirements approximately equal to precipitation) vegetation parcels referenced in the MND were sampled in 2025 and LAW118/129 in 2026. The reference parcels identified in the Plan were surveyed to characterize vegetation composition and perennial cover in undisturbed plant communities comparable to the Laws revegetation parcels, and specifically to measure the presence of Torrey’s saltbush and rubber rabbitbrush. Monitoring methods can be found in Appendix C. These parcels were also sampled by LADWP in 2023 and 2024 using a different method based on NRCS soil types but transects were not stratified randomly across the parcel. Future reference parcel monitoring methodologies will be jointly determined by LADWP and ICWD and brought to the Technical Group for approval.

title: Laws 2003 Plan Amendment (draft)
section: Additional Species outside of the MND recommendation
text:
Additional Species outside of the MND recommendation
The Plan provides project revegetation guidance, via two tables, that list the species to be planted in corresponding revegetation parcels. Table 1 lists species for parcels LAW090, 094 and 095, and Table 2 lists species to be planted in LAW118/129. The Plan states “Absent Technical Group approval, these species are the only ones that may be planted…” in these parcels. However, species not listed in the tables have either been planted in the parcels or have naturally recruited, predominantly along the planting rows where drip irrigation was provided, as these wetter soils were likely more conducive to recruitment. This amendment addresses two specific species, Torrey’s saltbush and rubber rabbitbrush, that LADWP planted in the revegetation parcels according to the planting schedule in Appendix F. The general use of irrigation to establish plants in mitigation projects will, by default, enhance the germination of species that respond to shallow groundwater; this unintended recruitment is likely unavoidable. Further, in desert ecosystems with high abiotic stress, it has been suggested that the role of facilitation (versus inter-species competition) in plant recruitment is underappreciated (He et al., 2013; Filazzola and Lortie, 2014), particularly the role of inter-species facilitation aiding the rehabilitation of disturbed environments (Zhao et al., 2006; Padilla and Pugnaire, 2006). Thus, the presence of “nurse species may facilitate the long-term recovery of native vegetation within the Laws parcels and may be acceptable in use if these nurse species represent the general species composition present at the landscape scale.

title: Laws 2003 Plan Amendment (draft)
text:
Field-data from Reference Parcels
To assess the extent of Torrey’s saltbush and rubber rabbitbrush vegetation cover present within Type A parcels in the Laws area, vegetation parcels referenced in the MND were sampled in 2025 and 2026. Two tables in the Plan’s Appendix II list the surrogate vegetation parcels used to generate both MND species planting lists, and the cover and composition goals: in Table A.1 for parcels LAW090, 094 and 095 and in Table A.2 for parcel LAW118/129. Cover and composition in 11 parcels are suggested to represent LAW090, 094 and 095, and nine parcels are listed to depict parcel LAW118/129.
LADWP used a method piloted between 2022-2024 to survey the parcels that would permit future comparison to remote sensing data derived from satellite imagery and during the growing season of 2025 and 2026. LADWP and ICWD sampled randomly stratified transects using this protocol. Supporting reference parcel data are provided in Appendix E.

text:
Results and Permitted Threshold Cover
For reference parcels associated with LAW090, 094, and 095, mean absolute cover was 0.1% for ATTO and 0.3% for ERNA10 (Table 2). For reference parcels associated with LAW118/129, mean absolute cover was 2.8% for ATTO and 4.3% for ERNA10 (Table 3).
These values provide an empirical basis for establishing upper limits on the allowable contribution of these species toward revegetation success. The permitted thresholds described below are informed by observed landscape-scale conditions and are not intended to replace or reduce the total perennial cover requirement established in the 2003 Plan.
Total perennial cover goals remain unchanged at 10% for all parcels. Inclusion of ATTO and ERNA10 is limited to the levels specified below to maintain consistency with the species composition framework of the original Plan.
Table 2. The MND reference parcels for LAW090, 094 and 095 surveyed in 2025; “Perennial” indicates the total perennial cover in the parcel, Torrey’s saltbush (Atriplex torreyi, species code = ATTO) and rubber rabbitbrush (Ericameria nauseosa, species code = ERNA10) are given as absolute percent.
Table 3. The MND reference parcels for LAW118/129 surveyed in 2025; “Perennial” indicates the total perennial cover in the parcel, while Torrey’s saltbush (Atriplex torreyi, species code = ATTO) and rubber rabbitbrush (Ericameria nauseosa, species code = ERNA10) are given as absolute percent cover.
Cattle saltbush (Atripex polycarpa), (species code = ATPO) is a dominant native perennial species in LAW118/129. The Plan’s table that lists recommended species for planting in Laws parcel LAW118/129 includes ATPO (Table 2), but also states “The NRCS potential ecological site gravely loam recommends no more than 3% of each of these species and no more than 15% in aggregate” referring to vegetation cover for the species listed in the planting table. ATPO cover recorded within LAW118/129 in 2025 was 3.5% and in 2026 was ?, exceeding that threshold. ATPO cover will be restricted to 3% cover maximum in LAW129/118.

title: Laws 2003 Plan Amendment (draft)
text:
Cover and Composition Goals
The presence of ATTO and ERNA10 on the landscape and the recorded average cover together inform a permitted threshold cover. Because ATTO and ERNA10 were documented within Type A parcels referenced for both species planting and cover and composition goals within the Plan, they will be allowed to be included under the following conditions:

LAW090, 094, 095

ATTO and ERNA10 vegetation cover can count 0.1% for ATTO and 0.3% for ERNA10 toward total perennial species cover for a combined total of 0.4% cover for the two species.
The total perennial cover goal for LAW090, 094, and 095 remains at 10%.
The composition goal will change; for each two species added to the permitted species list, one additional species is required, thus increasing to 11 species.



LAW118/129

LAW118/129 will be combined into one area, with 20 sections equally distributed across the parcels as detailed in the 2003 Plan.
ATTO and ERNA10 vegetation cover can count 2.8% for ATTO and 4.3% for ERNA10 toward a total perennial species cover for a combined total of 7.1% cover for the two species.
ATPO will be restricted to 3% vegetation cover as suggested by the Plan.
The total perennial cover goal for LAW118/129 remains at 10%.
The composition goal will change; for each two species added, the composition threshold will increase by one, thus increasing to 9 species. Any future adjustments to these limits would occur through the Technical Group process.

Once a parcel meets the initial criteria of both cover and composition, all revegetation activities, including irrigation, will be halted. For LAW090, 094, and 095, there will be a five-year deferment of all revegetation activities, including irrigation, before the parcel is reevaluated, and for LAW118/129 it will be eight-years deferment. This deferment period is to ensure that both composition and cover of the parcels can persist without intervention. During the deferment period, one of the years must be <80% of a normal precipitation year to account for drought conditions.
To be CEQA compliant, ERNA10 and ATTO will be conditionally added to the Plan’s species list. Once the species have been shown to persist and meet the goals above at the end of the deferment period, the species will be permanently added to the list.

title: Laws 2003 Plan Amendment (draft)
text:
Parcels not Meeting Goals
As of the writing of this document, parcels LAW094, 095, and 118/129 have not yet met revegetation goals and are considered in active revegetation status. Parcel LAW090 is currently meeting goals according to this amendment and will be assessed in 2027. Parcels will be evaluated when they appear to be reaching the modified goals.
When a parcel has met its revegetation goals:
The applicable rest period of all revegetation activities will commence.
If a parcel fails to meet the goals at the end of the respective rest period (five or eight years) of no revegetation activities, it will revert to active revegetation status with Technical Group approval.
Active revegetation status includes commencement of irrigation, maintenance, repair and replacement of irrigation infrastructure, planting containerized plants within low cover areas or where composition is lacking, and continued monitoring to assure the parcels are progressing towards the modified goals and to help guide revegetation efforts.
LADWP reserves the right to restart revegetation activities before completion of the rest period in consultation with the County.
Parcels that consistently fail to meet initial goals will be addressed by the Technical Group, and revegetation activities will be discussed. If revegetation efforts continue to fail, parcels will revert to irrigated agriculture per the Plan.

title: Laws 2003 Plan Amendment (draft)
text:
Clean Up Plan
Following a parcel being considered complete, a cleanup plan will be implemented. The cleanup plan will involve removing materials and equipment (e.g. t-posts, material stockpiles, bait stations, storage containers, heavy equipment). The perimeter fence will remain in place to limit grazing, vehicle access, and other potential disturbances. Following this, the open areas will be prepared for planting. Buried drip irrigation will be installed within the roads and open areas and will be planted with containerized plants listed in Tables 1 and 2 of the Plan. The newly planted areas will be monitored; sampled using the same protocol as described above in this amendment in conjunction with ICWD.

title: Laws 2003 Plan Amendment (draft)
text:
Unforeseen Disturbance
Depending on the status of a parcel, if affected by natural disaster (e.g. fire, debris flow, prolonged drought defined as two or more consecutive years of < 60% precipitation), remedial measures may be needed.
If the parcel is still in active revegetation status and has not met the modified goals, its status will remain active. This includes cleanup areas within a parcel.
For parcels that have met their initial goals and are under the rest period, evaluation using the monitoring protocols defined in this amendment will occur during the growing season after any disturbance.
If the goals are not met, the parcel will be reevaluated yearly for five years.
After five years, if it still does not meet the goals, it will return to active revegetation status.
If a parcel is deemed complete after the relative rest period and then disturbed, LADWP will not be responsible for revegetating the parcel, rather the parcels will be managed like LADWP land that has been affected by unforeseen disturbances. Any activities undertaken through this section will be done in consultation with the County.

title: Laws 2003 Plan Amendment (draft)
text:
Future Monitoring and Reporting
LADWP and ICWD will meet each spring to discuss monitoring and analysis of cover and species composition for the upcoming growing season, any planned revegetation efforts by LADWP, and to allocate staffing resources. Any future deviations from the Plan or this amendment will be brought to the attention of the County immediately so that the parties can work together to address the changes and reach mutual solutions. Results of this meeting and planned activities will be reported to the Technical Group.
Following joint monitoring of the parcels, LADWP and ICWD will jointly assess whether the parcels have met the modified goals. Parcels that have met goals will be identified along with the applicable rest period for each of those parcels specifying the date of commencement.
All applicable revegetation activities (including planting number and species) and monitoring results will be reviewed by ICWD and presented to the Technical Group for approval prior to being included in LADWP’s Owens Valley Annual Report. If the goals of the amendment are not being met, the Annual Report will identify areas where LADWP believes the revegetation goals cannot be timely and/or feasibly achieved and offer a revised plan to ensure completion.
The projects may be adaptively managed as alternative approaches become available to increase the rate and success of revegetation efforts. Project completion will be determined jointly by the County and LADWP.

title: State-and-transition model (STM) — draft
text:
Why STM here
A state-and-transition model (STM) describes the plant communities an ecological site can support, the transitions among them (management, drought, grazing, irrigation, etc.), and which changes are hard to reverse. ICWD’s broader Owens work lives in the stm repository (Green Book types as states within NRCS ecological sites; NMDS to test whether map types separate in species space).
For Laws Type E transfer parcels, the 2003 plan aims at a precipitation-dependent community after land leaves irrigated agriculture. Stock ESDs / STMs for upland desert sites usually start from native or lightly disturbed reference states. They rarely include an explicit abandoned irrigated agriculture state — bare or nearly bare ground where topsoil has blown away after years of cultivation and then stopping irrigation. That is the starting condition of LAW090 / 094 / 095 / 118 / 129 on the Green Book map (Type A · Barren Lands – Abag).

text:
Concept
Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) places samples in a low-dimensional map so that distances reflect community dissimilarity. Here each sample is a parcel–year; species values are relative cover (composition sums to 1). Dissimilarity is Bray–Curtis; ordination uses vegan::metaMDS — the same core pipeline as ICWD’s stm repo (code/nmds_functions.R).
Question for Type E: Do revegetation parcels (post-agricultural / ABAG starting points) sit apart from reference scrub parcels in species space? Do later years move toward the reference cloud?
Absolute cover magnitude is removed by row-normalization so the plot is about who is present in what proportions, not only how much total cover exists (compliance still uses absolute / capped cover on the revegetation page).

New relative to stock ESD STM: precip-only barren after irrigation ceases; organic/topsoil depleted; high wind erosion; low native cover


Early seral / assisted
Active revegetation: irrigation or drip, container stock, nurse species; cover rising but not yet self-sustaining


Reference-like A
Composition approaching Gravelly Loam arid reference (shadscale / saltbush / rabbitbrush mixes as on reference parcels)



Stock Gravelly Loam / Loamy 5-8” STMs still matter for within-scrub phases (grazing, annuals, shrub dominance). The ABAG box is the Type E transfer add-on: without it, the model pretends the site starts from a native barren or shrub state instead of post-agricultural erosion.

title: State-and-transition model (STM) — draft
text:
Purpose
What: A draft state-and-transition model (STM) for Laws Type E parcels: plant communities an ecological site can support, the transitions among them, and which changes are hard to reverse (Bestelmeyer et al. 2017).
Why: Cover and composition goals answer compliance; they do not name the starting state after irrigated agriculture ends. Stock desert STMs usually begin from native or lightly disturbed phases. Type E transfer parcels start as abandoned irrigated agriculture—often bare, with topsoil lost to wind after irrigation stops (Green Book Type A · Barren Lands – Abag). Without an explicit ABAG box, the model pretends recovery begins from intact scrub.
ICWD’s broader Owens STM work lives in stm (Green Book types as states within NRCS ecological sites; NMDS to test type separation).

title: NMDS — reference vs revegetation (draft)
text:
Purpose
What: Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) maps parcel–year samples so distances reflect community dissimilarity (McCune and Grace 2002). Species values are relative cover (row sums = 1); distance is Bray–Curtis; fitting uses vegan::metaMDS (Oksanen et al. 2024)—the same core pipeline as ICWD’s stm helpers.
Why: Compliance uses absolute (capped) cover. Relative composition asks a different question: do revegetation parcels (ABAG / early seral starts) sit apart from reference scrub in species space, and do later years move toward the reference cloud?2

title: Laws Type E Transfer Revegetation
text:
Purpose
What is Type E transfer? Land retired from irrigated agriculture (Green Book Type E) and managed toward a precipitation-dependent native community—not kept in farming (Inyo County and City of Los Angeles 1991; Los Angeles Department of Water and Power 2003b). This report tracks LAW090, LAW094, LAW095, and LAW118/129.
Why these metrics? Dryland succession can take decades; plan goals are milestones along that path, not proofs of climax. Absolute cover and richness answer compliance; STM and NMDS address ecological state and composition. Companion reference parcels supply empirical bases for ATTO/ERNA caps.1 Other 1991 EIR / 1999 Plan sites are reported separately (1999 Plan monitoring).
Default vs scenarios. Tables below use the working cap stack. Cap scenarios re-score the same hits under alternate cut points without replacing the primary analysis.

Revegetation targets (working rules)
All five must pass for overall attainment (✓ attained / ✗ not):

Perennial cover ≥ 10% — parcel mean of transect cover from allowable species (after caps).2
≥6 species with ≥3 hits — from allowable list plus ATTO, ERNA10, ATPO.
Species richness ≥ 10 — distinct perennial species from that same list.
Every transect ≥ 2% cover (same species filter).
≥1 grass species from the allowable list.

Working caps: LAW090/094/095 — ATTO and ERNA10 at 0.3% each (ATPO uncapped on LAW090). LAW118/129 — ATTO/ERNA10 2% each, ATPO 3%. Alternate stacks live in data/cap_scenarios.csv.
